body:
Tested locally on Linux, it resolves the black screen issue but introduces another issue. When I resize the window, I see a highly zoomed in version of the framebuffer (notice the sky background and its dithering pattern). This occurs regardless of whether I'm forcing MSAA through `nvidia-settings` or `__GL_FSAA_MODE=11 godot`.

I'm using the 4.x MRP from https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/18320#issue-316281106 for testing.

Before resizing:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cddcad09-2599-4be1-8142-c99c5c76b3be)

After resizing diagonally by a few pixels:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/52d432da-10e5-4bfa-bc6a-7a097c72eeec)

<details open>

<summary>PC specifications</summary>

- **CPU:** AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D
- **GPU:** NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090
- **RAM:** 64 GB (2×32 GB DDR5-6000 C30)
- **SSD:** Solidigm P44 Pro 2 TB
- **OS:** Linux (Fedora 42)
</details>

Tested locally, it works as expected. Code looks good to me.

Note that the MSAA level overridden by the graphics driver is not applied to the root Viewport (let alone SubViewports). It *will* technically apply to the main framebuffer, which is noticeable if you're forcing a MSAA level that contains SSAA, like here (pixels appear slightly blurry as a result):

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/77640aff-08d4-4d8e-89e9-43f287327403)

Compare this to when MSAA isn't forced:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/27f01222-1409-45a7-94f9-4f68572bdab5)

I'm not sure if we can make it so the driver will override the MSAA level in the root Viewport, which would make it behave closer to how forcing MSAA works on older OpenGL/D3D applications. I recall forcing MSAA in the driver worked correctly on Godot 2.x, but only sometimes…
